title: The neovim plugin installs from an nvim branch that the release script writes
body:
The neovim plugin lives in `editors/nvim/`, as `plugin/`, `ftdetect/`, `ftplugin/`, `syntax/`, `lua/acre/`, `tests/` and `README.md`. A plugin manager that installs from a git repo looks for those directories at the repo's root. Some managers can be pointed at a subdirectory. lazy.nvim cannot, and Jack uses it. A lazy user today has to clone acre and point `dir` at `editors/nvim`.

## Proposal

A branch named `nvim` has `editors/nvim/` at its root, and follows `main`. A lazy user installs the plugin with one line:

```lua
{ "jackroddy/acre", branch = "nvim" }
```

`scripts/push-release` writes `nvim`, and nobody commits to it by hand. The script runs `git subtree split --prefix=editors/nvim main`, then pushes `main`, its tags and the split to `nvim` in one atomic push. `CLAUDE.md` says to push every release with the script. `editors/nvim/` stays the place to edit the plugin, and to install it locally or by hand.

The split produces the same commit from the same history, and the split of later history descends from the split of earlier history, so each release fast-forwards `nvim`. A push that would not fast-forward fails, and `main` stays where it was.

## Rejected

- A GitHub Actions workflow that splits on each push to `main`. It would also cover a push to `main` made without the script, but `main` moves only at a release, and Jack cuts every release. A workflow needs a prototype cycle on GitHub, plus `contents: write` and full-history checkout.
- A pre-push hook. It runs before the push of `main` is accepted. A push from inside the hook fires the hook again. Hooks are not versioned, so each clone has to install it.
- Branch protection on `nvim`. The branch is cheap to rewrite, so a stray push gets fixed by hand.

## Cost

- The Branches and Releases sections of `CLAUDE.md` name `nvim` and the script.
- The plugin's README gives the lazy line.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cac6cd1d
notes.text:
Jack settled the open questions.

- `main` feeds `nvim`, so lazy users get the plugin at a release, in step with acre-gui.
- No branch protection on `nvim`. The branch is cheap to rewrite, so a stray push gets fixed by hand.
- The plugin's README gives the lazy line once the branch exists.

The costs listed are expected: the first workflow in the repo, and a line in the Branches section of `CLAUDE.md`. Once this lands, falx gets an issue that describes how to copy the setup.
